import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Badge } from './Badge' import * as BadgeStories from './Badge.stories' # Badge A small count or dot that flags something new on another element: unread messages on an inbox, a status on an avatar. ## Variants Each variant comes as a count or, with `isDot`, a dot. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `primary` | The default: new items in the brand colour. | | `accent` | Strong and neutral, where the brand colour would clash. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: a total, not news. As a dot, Offline. | | `destructive` | Something needs attention: failures, overdue items. As a dot, Busy. | | `success` | As a dot, Online. | | `warning` | As a dot, Away or Pending. | `maxCount` keeps a large number from stretching the badge past its anchor. `isFloating` pins the badge to a corner of the element it wraps. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/badge.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Badge.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/badge](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/badge) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The anchor only exists when the badge has `children`. A badge on its own is just the container. ## Measurements `md` is the xs control tier (Foundations / Sizing). Both sizes keep a single digit a circle: the minimum width equals the height. `sm` pads the count by 2px either side, below the spacing scale on purpose. A floating badge is centred on its corner of the anchor, half in and half out, with a 2px ring. ## Color A dot has no text to carry it, so it must reach 3:1 against the page on its own. That is why the `secondary` and `warning` dots step to a darker colour than their pill. ## States A badge is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. Its states are what it shows. }, { label: 'Over maxCount', content: }, { label: 'Zero', content: }, { label: 'Dot', content: }, ]} /> `count={0}` shows "0". Hide the badge yourself if nothing new should mean no badge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the badge, not to the anchor. ### Differences from the spec - **`children` is added.** A floating badge needs something to float on. The badge wraps it in a `position: relative` span rather than asking every consumer to position the anchor themselves. - **`accent` is the inverted neutral.** The token set has one brand hue, which `primary` already uses, so `accent` is foreground-on-background: the strongest contrast available without inventing a colour. - **`success` and `warning` are added** from the status tokens, for presence and state dots. - **`floatingPlacement` defaults to `top-end`**, the usual notification corner; the spec gives no default. - **Start and end are physical** (left and right). RTL pages would get mirrored placement. ## When to use Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar. A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on carries the meaning in its own name. } doCaption="The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too." dont={} dontCaption="The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”." /> Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or a name beside it. ## When not to use - **For a label or category.** Use a [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words, a badge holds a number. - **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast. - **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything is, nothing stands out. ## Accessibility - An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12"). - A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside* the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead: `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`. - A **dot** has no text and is hidden too. - Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`. - Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

Above {children} Below
) # Divider A thin line that separates content into groups: sections of a card, items in a toolbar, blocks of a page. ## Variants | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `solid` | Almost everywhere: the quiet default. | | `dashed` | A boundary that is softer or provisional: a drop zone, a "more below" break, a draft section. | A **vertical** divider separates items in a row: toolbar groups, links in a footer. It has no fixed height and stretches to its flex row. **Inset** stops the line short of the container's edges, so it aligns with the text in a padded list rather than running edge to edge. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/divider.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Divider.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/divider](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/divider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy One part. The line is a border, top for horizontal and start for vertical, and the box shrinks to it: a vertical divider is exactly as wide as its line. ## Measurements Thickness is whole pixels, not a token: the token layer has no border-width scale, and a rule should stay a crisp pixel at every `--scaling`. | Size | Thickness | | --- | --- | | `sm` | 1px | | `md` | 2px | | `lg` | 4px | ## Color Every size and appearance uses the same colour. ## States A divider is not interactive: no hover, focus or pressed. It looks the same whether it is announced or decorative; only a screen reader tells them apart. }, { label: 'Dashed', content: }, { label: 'Inset', content: }, { label: 'Decorative', content: }, ]} /> ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref` and `aria-hidden`. ### Differences from the spec - **`appearance`, not `variant`.** In this kit `variant` always means a colour by intent (primary, destructive…) and `appearance` means a style. Solid versus dashed is a style. - **Thickness is raw px.** The token layer has no border-width scale, and a divider is the only component that needs three. ## When to use Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar. Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see. } doCaption="One line between two groups: the break carries meaning." dont={} dontCaption="A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group." /> ## When not to use - **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise. - **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space. - **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own border, not a Divider beside it. ## Accessibility - `
` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is already the default. - If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all. - The `--border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Tag } from './Tag' import * as TagStories from './Tag.stories' # Tag A short label that categorises or marks something: a status, a filter chip, a person picked in a field. ## Variants `variant` is the colour: a status, or a hue for categories. `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | A plain label with no status: a type, a version. | | | Informational status: In review, Scheduled. The default. | | | Done or healthy: Paid, Verified, Live. | | | Needs attention soon: Expiring, Pending. | | | Failed or blocked: Overdue, Error. | | | A hue: one per category, label or owner. It carries no meaning. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | | Most places: a tint that sits in a row of text. | | | Dense tables and busy surfaces, where many tints would be loud. | | | One tag that must stand out: a single status on a card. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tag } from 'zweihander/tag' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tag.json ``` - Source: [src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/atomic-elements/Tag.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tag](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tag) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy ## Measurements A tag sits in a line of text, so each size reads the control tier below its name (Foundations / Sizing): `md` is tier sm, `sm` is tier xs. A 1px padding and a 1px border, transparent unless outlined, make up the tier's height, so appearances never shift the layout. The corner follows the Theme's radius preset like every control: a pill under `radius="full-rounded"`. ## Color Each variant has a solid, a colour on that solid, a subtle tint and a text colour that subtle and outlined use. Subtle and outlined text is measured at 4.5:1 by the token build. Every hue follows the same four tokens under its own name. Red, as an example; the other sixteen swap `red` for their hue. ## States The tag itself is not interactive. Its remove button is: - **Hover** tints the button with the tag's own text colour at 15%, so it reads on every variant and appearance without a token for each. - **Focus** is the `--ring` outline every control uses, drawn inset so it stays inside a 20px tag. - Pressing removes nothing by itself: `onRemove` reports it, and the parent drops the tag from its list. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Checkbox } from './Checkbox' import * as CheckboxStories from './Checkbox.stories' # Checkbox Selects an option, or several from a list, to apply when a form is submitted. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the checked box. Each row: unchecked, checked, indeterminate. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The default: lists, forms, tables. The checked box is the foreground colour, so a column of them stays calm. | | | One checkbox that carries the brand: an opt-in, a terms box beside a primary button. | **Indeterminate** is for a parent whose children are partly selected. It is a display state: clicking the parent chooses all or none, never "mixed". ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/checkbox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Checkbox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/checkbox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/checkbox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Checkbox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/checkbox) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The label wraps the box, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The box is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits centred on the first line of its label, however many lines the label wraps to. The box's corner is the radius step, not the control tier's radius: a box that turned round under `radius="full-rounded"` would read as a radio. ## Color ## States }, { label: 'Indeterminate', content: }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on the label darkens an unchecked outline to `--foreground`. A checked box mixes 12% of the mark's colour into its fill, as Button does. An error outline stays red. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the box. - **Disabled** dims the box and the label to 50%. - **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the box. ### Differences from the spec - **Base UI's and HTML's names:** `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange` for the spec's `defaultValue` (a string there, which reads as the submitted value: that is `value`) and `onChange`; native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` for the `is…` forms. - **`isIndeterminate` keeps its prefix.** Indeterminate is a DOM property, not an HTML attribute, so by the kit's naming rule it takes `is`; Base UI calls it `indeterminate`. - **`autoFocus` is applied on mount by the component.** The box is a focusable ``, which React's own `autoFocus` ignores. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as checked, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship. ## When to use Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens until the form is sent. Write the label so that checked means yes. } doCaption="The label says what checking does: checked means yes." dont={} dontCaption="A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out." /> ## When not to use - **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit. - **For one choice out of several.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes are independent. - **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate. Space toggles it. - The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box. - `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets `aria-invalid`. - The unchecked outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page on every gray ramp. - A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form submission and validation. - 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers, without the box growing.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { ColorPicker } from './ColorPicker' import * as ColorPickerStories from './ColorPicker.stories' # Color Picker Chooses a colour: type it in any CSS format, pick a swatch, find it on a saturation and brightness area and a hue strip, or type its channels in Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB. The panel is laid out like Figma's colour picker. ## Variants Two exports. | Export | Use for | | --- | --- | | `ColorPicker` | A form field: the hex in a text field, with a swatch button that opens the panel in a popover. | | `ColorPanel` | The panel on its own, always open: a sidebar, an inspector, a settings page about colour. | `alpha` adds opacity; `defaultFormat` picks which channels the fields show first. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ColorPicker, ColorPanel } from 'zweihander/color-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/color-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/ColorPicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/color-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/color-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) and [Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The panel here is shown open under its field; in a `ColorPicker` it opens in a popover from the swatch button. ## Measurements The field is a Text Input: the same tiers, padding and label. The panel is the same at both field sizes. The panel is 16rem wide, so eight swatches fit in a row, and the area is 10rem tall. The format menu and the channels are the kit's md (32px) Select and field box. ## Color The area, the hue strip and the checkerboard are the colour model itself, so they are fixed colours, not theme tokens. The thumbs are white rings with a dark edge: one of the two is at least 3:1 against whatever colour is under them. Swatches have a faint inner edge, black 10% in light mode and white 10% in dark, as in Figma. That is below the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11 round a white swatch on white, accepted because the hex in the field, not the edge, tells the colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** follows Text Input on the field. In the panel every thumb, swatch and field draws a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside. - **Disabled** dims the field and disables the swatch button. - **Error** is Text Input's. Typed text that is not a colour turns the field to error on its own, with a hint, and keeps the last good value. - **Chosen swatch** has a 2px `--primary` ring; focused as well, the ring turns `--ring` and moves 1px further out. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ColorPanel` takes `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `alpha`, `defaultFormat`, `swatches`, `disabled` and `className`. `parseColor(text)` reads any CSS colour (`rgb(59 130 246)`, `hsl(217 91% 60% / 50%)`, `oklch(...)`, `rebeccapurple`) to the same hex, or `null`; the browser parses it, so outside one only hex is read. `normalizeHex(text)` turns `#abc`, `ABC` or `#AABBCC` into `#aabbcc`, keeps an alpha byte (`#3b82f680`, or `#abc8` as `#aabbcc88`) unless it is `ff`, and turns anything else into `null`. ### Design notes - **Hex in, hex out.** The value is lowercase `#rrggbb`, with an alpha byte only while opacity is under 100%. Typed text is read on Enter or blur: hex of 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits with or without `#`, or any CSS colour. It is shown back as hex. - **Formats are a view, not a value.** RGB, HSL and HSB only change the fields; the value stays hex. Channel fields commit on Enter or blur, and up and down step by 1 (Shift by 10), as in a design tool. - **The hue is remembered.** The picker keeps hue, saturation and brightness, so dragging to black and back leaves the hue strip where it was instead of jumping to red. - **Not in this version:** Figma's library picker ("On this page"), gradients and an eyedropper. ## When to use Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow, offer it as named swatches. } doCaption="The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex." dont={} dontCaption="A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off." /> ## When not to use - **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag colours, a theme accent), use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour. - **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text. ## Accessibility - The field is a text input named by its label. The swatch button is named "Choose colour, #3b82f6 selected", and the popover is a dialog named "Choose colour" that returns focus to the button on Escape. - The area is one tab stop: a slider named "Saturation" whose value text reads both numbers ("Saturation 76%, brightness 96%"). Left and right change saturation, up and down brightness, Shift moves 10%, Page Up and Page Down change brightness by 10%, Home and End set saturation to 0 or 100%. A second "Brightness" slider is there for a screen reader's browse mode. - The hue strip is a slider named "Hue", read as "217 degrees"; the opacity strip, "Opacity", read as "50%". - The format menu is the kit's Select, named "Colour format". Channel fields are text inputs named for what they hold ("Red", "Hue degrees", "Lightness percent", "Opacity percent", "Hex"), so they do not share a name with the sliders. - Swatches are native radios in a radio group named "Swatches": one tab stop, arrows move and choose, and the chosen one is checked. None is checked while the colour is not one of them. They are 24px with 8px between them, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 without a larger invisible target. - A colour is never the only way to know the value: the hex is always in the field.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { RadioGroup } from './Radio' import * as RadioStories from './Radio.stories' # Radio Chooses exactly one option from a short list, all visible at once. The component is `RadioGroup`. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the selected radio; `orientation` lays the options out in a column or a row. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `neutral` | The default: forms and settings. The selected radio is the foreground colour. | | `primary` | A choice that carries the brand: a plan picker beside a primary button. | | Orientation | Use for | | --- | --- | | `vertical` | The default. Options with helper text, or labels longer than a word or two. | | `horizontal` | Two to four short labels: sizes, yes or no. The row wraps when narrow. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/radio.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Radio.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Radio.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/radio](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/radio) - Behaviour: [Base UI Radio Group](https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio), [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) and [Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each option's label wraps its radio, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements One size. The circle is control tier xs (Foundations / Sizing) and sits centred on the first line of its label. The legend is the body size at medium weight. ## Color An option's own helper describes the option, so it stays muted when the group is in error or success; only the group message takes that colour. ## States }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** anywhere on an option's label darkens an unselected ring to `--foreground`. The selected radio mixes 12% of the dot's colour into its fill, as Button does. An error ring stays red. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the circle. - **Disabled** dims the radio and its label to 50%, for the whole group or one option. - **Read-only** looks enabled but has no hover and an arrow cursor. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the group. ### Differences from the spec - **The component is the group.** The spec describes a single radio, but a radio means nothing alone: selection, arrow keys and the single tab stop all belong to the group. Following the kit's "flat props" convention, the radios are `options` rather than child components. - **`checked` and `autoFocus` per radio are not props.** The group's `value` says which is checked. - Base UI's `onValueChange` and native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` names, as on Checkbox. - **No `secondary`.** A light fill barely reads as selected, so only `neutral` (the foreground colour) and `primary` ship, as on Checkbox. ## When to use Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one. } doCaption="A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected." dont={} dontCaption="Ten radios are a wall to scan. A long list belongs in a Select or a Combobox." /> ## When not to use - **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on screen.** Use a Select, or a Combobox when the reader knows what to type. - **For several choices at once.** Use [Checkboxes](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs). - **For a single on or off.** Use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) in a form, or a [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs) for a setting that applies at once. ## Accessibility - A `
` with a ``, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by the legend. - **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options are skipped. - Each option's helper text is its own description. Plain group help describes the group once; an error message reaches every radio, so whichever has focus says what is wrong. - The unselected outline is `--control-border`, 3:1 on the page. - A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form submission and validation. - 44×44px touch target on each radio on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Rating } from './Rating' import * as RatingStories from './Rating.stories' # Rating Asks for, or shows, a score out of a few stars: a review, a template's rating, a difficulty. ## Variants A rating either asks for a score or shows one. | Mode | Use for | | --- | --- | | | Asking: a review form, rating a template. Whole stars only. | | | Showing: an average beside a product. Fractions draw as a star filled part-way. | `getValueText` changes what each score is called, for a scale that is not stars: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Rating } from 'zweihander/rating' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/rating.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Rating.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Rating.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/rating](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/rating) - Behaviour: native radio buttons; no Base UI part covers it - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each star is a label over an invisible native radio, so arrows, Tab and form submission are the browser's own. Read-only drops the radios: the stars are one image. ## Measurements Stars sit 2px apart, below the spacing scale on purpose, as on Tag. The label is medium weight. ## Color The fill is the bright `--warning` amber, not the darker warning text colour: a rating reads as a rating when it looks like one. It is 2.1:1 on white, below the 3:1 a meaningful graphic needs, so colour is not what carries the score. A filled star differs from the outlined empty one by shape, and the group or image is named "3 out of 5 stars". ## States }, { label: 'Unrated', content: }, { label: 'Read-only', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** previews the score up to the star under the pointer, and only while the rating can be changed. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline round the focused star. - **Disabled** dims the stars to 50%. - **Read-only** is one image; fractions fill a star part-way, cut rather than shrunk. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`className` passes through to the group. ## When to use Use a rating to ask for, or show, a quick score on a short scale: a review, a difficulty, how useful something was. Keep the scale short: five stars is the convention readers already know. } doCaption="Five stars: few enough to hit and to tell apart at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Ten stars are small targets, and 7 looks much like 8. Use a Slider or a Number Input for a fine scale." /> ## When not to use - **For a precise number.** Use a [Slider](?path=/docs/components-controls-slider--docs) or a Number Input. - **For a choice between named options.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so the options say what they mean. - **To show progress.** Use a Progress Bar. ## Accessibility - Interactive: a `
` named by its legend (or `aria-label`), with one radio per star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words with `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of the group. - Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars". - Hover previews the score; focus shows the 2px ring round the star. - A filled star differs from an empty one by shape as well as colour. - Stars grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

Off is the same in every variant. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | | The default: most settings. | | | Neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | | A setting that is risky to leave on: public sharing, deleting old data automatically. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Switch } from 'zweihander/switch' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/switch.json ``` - Source: [src/components/controls/Switch.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/controls/Switch.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/switch](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/switch) - Behaviour: [Base UI Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch) and [Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The label wraps the track, so the whole label is part of the click target. ## Measurements Track heights are 16, 20 and 24px; `md` and `lg` are control tiers xs and sm (Foundations / Sizing). Each track is about one and three quarter heights wide, so the thumb travels most of a thumb-width. The thumb sits 2px inside the track at every size. ## Color Off is a `--control-border` track (3:1 on the page, so the control is visible at all) with a page-coloured thumb. On takes the variant's solid, and the thumb its label colour, measured at 4.5:1 against it. ## States }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus-visible' }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, { label: 'Error', content: }, ]} > - **Hover** changes only the cursor: the track has no lighter or darker step to move to without losing its 3:1. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the track. - **Disabled** dims the track and the label to 50%. - **Error** draws a 2px `--danger-text` edge inside the track, so it reads on and off alike and leaves the band outside to the focus ring. - **Read-only** looks enabled, with an arrow cursor. - The thumb slides over `--duration-base`, and stops animating under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`id`, `className`, `aria-label` and `ref` pass through to the track. ### Differences from the spec - **Base UI's names:** `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` for the spec's `defaultValue` and `onChange`; native `disabled`, `required`, `readOnly` for `isDisabled`, `isRequired`, `isReadOnly`. - **`helperText` is added.** `validationState="error"` needs somewhere to say what is wrong; colour alone is not a message. ## When to use Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped, like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save. } doCaption="The setting applies as soon as the switch moves." dont={} dontCaption="A switch that waits for Save looks done when it is not. Use a checkbox in a form." /> ## When not to use - **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs). - **For more than two options.** Use a [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select. - **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). Use a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs). ## Accessibility - `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it. - The label wraps the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it. - `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the error state the switch has `aria-invalid`. - The off track is `--control-border`, measured at 3:1 on the page on every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both states. - A hidden `` carries `name`, `value` and `required` into native form submission and validation. - On is the end side: in a right-to-left page the thumb travels left. - 44×44px touch target on coarse pointers.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Calendar } from './Calendar' import * as CalendarStories from './Calendar.stories' # Calendar A month grid to pick one day from, or to show one: a booking page, the inside of a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs). ## Variants Calendar has one look and one size. What changes is what it shows. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | One day (`value`) | Picking or showing a single day: a delivery date, a booking. | | A span (`range`) | Showing a stay or a report period. Clicks still report one day; Date Range Picker decides the span. | | Limits (`min`, `max`) | Booking windows: nothing before tomorrow, nothing after the season ends. | | Ruled-out days (`isDateDisabled`) | Weekends, holidays, days already booked. | | Locale (`locale`, `weekStartsOn`) | Month and weekday names in the reader's language, and their first day of the week. | The locale decides the week: `vi-VN` and `en-GB` start on Monday, `en-US` on Sunday, read from `Intl.Locale` where the browser knows it (Monday otherwise). The grid is always Gregorian, so a locale whose own calendar is not (Persian) still gets Gregorian days, in its own digits. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/calendar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Calendar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/calendar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/calendar) - Behaviour: a plain element, using `Intl` for names and the week's first day: no date library - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The grid always has six rows. Months span four to six weeks; a fixed height keeps a popover or a page from jumping as you page through them. Two more looks sit on the days: **today**, an orange disc, round where a selected day takes the control's corners; and with `range`, the **band**, as tall as a day, behind the days between the two ends. The band rounds off where a week or the month starts or ends. Days of the months either side are never banded, so two months side by side never draw the same day twice. ## Measurements Calendar has one size. Days are 32px, 4px apart: each cell pads by half of `--space-1` on every side, so a range's band runs unbroken under the gap. Figures are tabular, so the columns of dates line up. On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) days grow to 44px, the touch target; the previous and next buttons stay 32px. ## Color One table per kind of day. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - **Day** has no fill at rest. - **Today's figure is dark**, not white: white on `--orange` is 3.4:1, under the 4.5:1 a 14px figure needs, while `--orange-contrast` clears 4.9:1 in both modes. A selected today shows as selected. - **Outside days** are `--muted-foreground` mixed 50% with transparent, about 2:1. No token is lighter, and WCAG allows it for decoration: they are hidden from assistive tech and cannot be picked. - **Unavailable days** are struck through as well as faded, so they do not rely on colour. ## States }, { label: 'Today', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every day at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** fills a day, or the previous and next buttons, with `--accent` behind `--accent-foreground`. The selected day and today keep their own colours; unavailable and outside days do not react. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the day. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click selects the day, and the selected look follows. - **Disabled** is per day: before `min`, after `max`, or ruled out by `isDateDisabled`. The previous and next buttons disable at the limits, at 50% opacity. - **Selected** is the brand fill, with the control's corners; **today** is the orange disc, round. With `range`, both ends are selected and the days between are banded. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Also exported, for working with the same plain dates: `isSameDay`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `startOfDay`, `firstDayOfWeek` and the `DateRange` type. Every date is local midnight; times are ignored. ## When to use Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than refusing the choice after it is made. } doCaption="A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them." dont={} dontCaption="A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker." /> Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28 February, not 3 March. ## When not to use - **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs): it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted. - **For a span inside a form.** Use a [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs): it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here. - **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content. List the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs). ## Accessibility - A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`. - Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September 2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`. - One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected. - Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends, Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the next one. - Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day) and the previous and next chevrons are mirrored. - The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced. - The previous and next buttons are named "Previous month" and "Next month", and are disabled at `min` and `max`. - Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does nothing. - Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from assistive tech. - Today's figure measures at least 4.5:1 on its disc, in both modes, on its own and inside a range.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as CarouselStories from './Carousel.stories' # Carousel A row of slides seen one (or a few) at a time: featured items, a gallery, onboarding cards. ## Variants The carousel has no `variant` prop. These are its configurations: | Configuration | Use for | | --- | --- | | One in view (default) | Large slides that each need the full width: a feature, a photo. | | `slidesPerView={3}` | Smaller items browsed in a row: templates, products. | | `loop` | A short set with no natural first or last, where next from the end should wrap. | | `autoPlay` | Rarely. A showcase where motion is the point; it adds a stop/start button. | With three in view, five slides have three stops (1-3, 2-4, 3-5), and the dots count stops, not slides. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Carousel } from 'zweihander/carousel' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/carousel.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Carousel.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/carousel](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/carousel) - Behaviour: [WAI-ARIA carousel pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The controls sit above the track, at its end, so they never cover a slide. A visually hidden line after the track says where the reader is (see Accessibility). - **Native scrolling.** No transform maths and no gesture library: the track is `overflow-x: auto` with `scroll-snap-type`, so touch, trackpad and momentum behave as the platform does. import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TableStories from './Table.stories' # Table Rows of records with the same fields, to scan and compare: projects, invoices, members. Columns can sort, rows can be selected and expanded. ## Variants Any table takes any of these together: a selectable table can also expand its rows and keep its header in view. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `density="md"` | The default, 48px rows: most tables, and rows that hold a Tag or a button. | | `density="sm"` | 40px rows, for long lists of plain text where seeing more rows at once matters. | | `isSelectable` | Acting on several rows at once: archive, export, assign. | | `expandedContent` | Details that belong to one row but do not fit in a column: a description, a timeline, line items. | | `hasStickyHeader` | Long tables that scroll inside a fixed height, so the column names stay in view. | | `emptyState` | Saying why there are no rows, and what to do: clear a search, add the first one. | Rows with details open under themselves. Expansion is independent of selection and survives sorting: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Table, type TableColumn } from 'zweihander/table' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/table.json ``` - Source: [src/components/data-display/Table.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/data-display/Table.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/table](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/table) - Behaviour: a native ``; selection uses the kit's [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs), expansion its [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The table sits in a container that scrolls sideways on a narrow screen rather than squeezing the columns. The selection column comes first, then the expand column; a row whose `expandedContent` returns nothing leaves its expand cell empty. ## Measurements Each density is a row height. Everything else is the same in both. Rows are divided by a 1px rule; the last row has none. The sort button pulls itself out by its own inline padding, so its label lines up with the cells below. Figures are tabular, so numbers line up column-wide. ## Color Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. - Rows are not striped: the dividers separate them. - The sort icon of a column that is not sorted is the label's colour at 60% opacity. - **Between two selected rows** the divider is mixed from the tint: `--primary-subtle` with a quarter of `--primary-subtle-text`. `--border` is as light as the tint in light mode and would vanish. - **An open row and its content read as one block**: no divider between them, and the content row shares its row's hover and selected tint. ## States }, { label: 'Selected', content: }, ]} /> }]} /> Each example forces the state on every row and button at once; on screen it is the one under the pointer or the keyboard. - **Hover** tints the row with `--accent`, and the sort button too. The content row of an open row takes no hover of its own, only its row's. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, drawn 2px inside the sort button. The checkboxes and the expand button keep their own focus rings. - **Pressed** has no look of its own: the click sorts, selects or opens, and that state's look follows. - **Disabled**: Table has none. A row that cannot be acted on is a row without the control. - **Sorted** shows the column's icon at full colour, pointing up or down. - **Selected** tints the row with `--primary-subtle`. - **Expanded** turns the chevron to point down and opens the content row under it. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TableColumn` describes one column: - `key`: unique; also the row field shown when there is no `cell`. - `header`: the column's label. - `cell`: renders the cell; defaults to `row[key]`. - `sortable`: adds a sort button to the header. It sorts by `sortValue`, or by `row[key]`. - `align`: `start`, `center` or `end`. `end` for numbers and dates, so the digits line up. - `width`: any CSS width, e.g. `8rem` or `20%`. - `isRowHeader`: makes the column's cells `
`, the name a row is known by. Usually the first column. `TableSort` is `{ key, direction }`, with direction `ascending` or `descending`. ## When to use Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`. } doCaption="Numbers and dates aligned to the end, in tabular figures: the digits line up column-wide." dont={} dontCaption="Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance." /> } doCaption="A row header names each row, so its checkbox reads “Select Atlas”." dont={} dontCaption="Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select." /> **Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled, the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways. With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the rows already sorted: **Paging is not built in.** Put a [Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only. Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table: ## When not to use - **For a whole list page** with search, filters, bulk actions and paging. Start from the [Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs) pattern, which puts a Table together with them. - **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs). - **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader; use CSS grid to place things side by side. - **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit has no data grid yet. ## Accessibility - A real `` named by its `
`, with `
` headers and a `` for the row header column: screen readers announce the column and the row for every cell. - Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header. - Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`. - Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"), reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state. - A row with nothing to expand has no button. - The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column is announced like the others. - The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its row.

) # Combobox A field you type into to filter a list of options, then choose one. ## Variants Two sizes, and the field's validation states. Typing filters the list and marks the match; the chosen option carries a check. | Size | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Forms and settings: the default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a toolbar filter, a table row, beside `sm` buttons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/combobox.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/Combobox.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/combobox](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/combobox) - Behaviour: [Base UI Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The options list opens under the field, at least as wide as it: - **Option**: the label, with the typed text marked by weight and underline. The typed order follows `locale`: day first in `en-GB` and `vi-VN`, month first in `en-US`. The form always gets `yyyy-mm-dd`. | Locale | Typed as | | --- | --- | | `en-GB`, `vi-VN` | `dd/mm/yyyy` | | `en-US` | `mm/dd/yyyy` | `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled` limit what can be picked or typed: For a span of days, see [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs). ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The calendar opens in a popover 4px under the field, aligned to its start: a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) in a panel. Its days, header and paging buttons are specified there. ## Measurements The field is the kit's field: each size is a control tier, with the normal inline padding and the field radius. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. The popover never grows wider than the screen less 16px a side. ## Color The field's edge is a light hairline, about 1.5:1: an approved exception to WCAG 1.4.11, as on every kit field. The calendar's own colours are on its page. ## States }, { label: 'Filled' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' }, { label: 'Error', content: , }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the field, drawn while the input has focus, by pointer too. In the error state the ring is `--danger-text`. The calendar button draws its own ring when tabbed to. - **Error** turns the edge and the helper `--danger-text`. It is also shown on its own while the typed text is not a date, or is outside `min` and `max`: the helper then gives the expected pattern. - **Hover** changes nothing on the field; the calendar icon darkens from `--muted-foreground` to `--foreground`. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity; the calendar button is disabled with it. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Typing is first-class.** Many people type a known date faster than they can page to it. Any separator works (`3.10.26`, `3/10/2026`); the field reformats on blur or Enter. - **An impossible date is kept, not guessed.** `31/02/2026` stays as typed, the field turns to its error state and the helper shows the expected pattern; nothing is reported until it is a real date. - **A click in the input opens the calendar, and keeps focus there.** Typing carries on with the month in view; the calendar button and Alt+Down move focus into the calendar instead. - **The form gets ISO.** Whatever the display order, `name` submits `yyyy-mm-dd`, so the server never has to guess the locale. ### Differences from the spec - **`onValueChange`, not `onChange`**, with a `Date` or `null`, as the kit's other value fields. ## When to use Use a Date Picker for one date: a start date, a due date, a booking. Let people type it when they know it, and pick it when they want to see the week around it. Set `min`, `max` or `isDateDisabled` so a date that cannot be used cannot be chosen, rather than refusing it after submit. } doCaption="The empty field shows the pattern to type, in the locale's order." dont={} dontCaption="An example date as the placeholder reads as a value already filled in." /> ## When not to use - **For a span of days.** Use a [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs): one field, both ends, never back to front. - **To show a month on the page.** Use a [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) inline. - **For a time of day.** The picker holds a date only. ## Accessibility - The input is a labelled text box with `inputmode="numeric"` for a number keypad; while the text is not a valid date it has `aria-invalid` and the helper explains the format. - The calendar button is named "Choose date", with the current date when there is one. Alt+Down in the input opens it too. - The calendar opens as a dialog named "Choose date" with focus on the selected day; Escape closes it without a change. - **After a pick the field goes back to rest.** Picked with the pointer, focus leaves the field (no caret, no ring), as in Combobox. Picked with the keyboard, focus returns to where it came from (the button, or the input), so keyboard and screen reader users are not dropped to the page. - The field and calendar's own labels ("Choose date", "Previous month") are in English, like the rest of the kit's built-in labels. - On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the calendar button gets a 44×44px hit area without the field growing.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { DateRangePicker } from './DatePicker' import * as DateRangePickerStories from './DateRangePicker.stories' # Date Range Picker A field for a span of days: a report period, a booking. Typed like [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs), or picked from two months side by side. ## Variants Two sizes, `sm` and `md`, and the field's validation states, as on Date Picker. With `presets`, whole periods sit beside the calendars. | Option | Use for | | --- | --- | | No presets | Ranges that rarely line up with a calendar period: a booking, a leave request. | | `presets` | Reports and filters, where people mostly want "Last month" or "This year". | ## Resources Shipped in the same file as Date Picker, which it shares its field and popover with. From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { DateRangePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/date-picker.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/DatePicker.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/date-picker](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/date-picker) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover), and the kit's [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The popover holds: - **Presets**, with `presets`: whole periods, Today to Last year, in a column beside the calendars, or a row above them on a narrow screen. - **Calendars**: two months that page on their own, opening on the range's first and last months (this month and the next when empty). The left one always stays before the right: paging one past the other pushes the other along. One month on a screen narrower than 40rem. ## Measurements The field is Date Picker's: each size is a control tier, with the normal inline padding and the field radius. Presets are 2px apart and at least 7rem wide in the column. The field is 20rem wide unless `isFullWidth`; a range is longer than one date, so give it room or `isFullWidth`. ## Color The days and the band between the range's ends are the [Calendar](?path=/docs/components-data-display-calendar--docs)'s colours. ## States }, { label: 'Filled' }, { label: 'Focus', pseudo: 'focus' }, { label: 'Error', content: , }, { label: 'Disabled', content: , }, ]} > The field's states are Date Picker's: a `--ring` outline while the input has focus, `--danger-text` in error (also while the typed text is not a range), 50% opacity when disabled. A preset matching the picked range stays in its pressed look. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Either way round.** The first click starts the range, the second ends it; a second click before the first swaps them. So does typing the later date first. - **Presets are whole periods.** "This month" is the 1st to the last day, not the 1st to today, so a preset reads the same all month. - **No Cancel or Apply.** A range applies, and the popover closes, once both ends are in; Escape before the second click leaves the value as it was. - **No hover preview.** The band shows once both ends are in; add a preview if testing shows people lose track of the first click. ## When to use Use a Date Range Picker when the two dates are one thing: a period to report on, a stay, a sprint. Both ends are set together, start never after end, and the value is complete or `null`. } doCaption="One field for one period: it cannot be half filled or set back to front." dont={} dontCaption="Two Date Pickers for one period: here the end is before the start, and nothing stops it." /> ## When not to use - **For one date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs). - **When one end is optional**, such as a contract with no end date. The range needs both ends; use two Date Pickers and check their order yourself. ## Accessibility - As Date Picker: a labelled text box, an error state with the expected pattern, and the calendars in a dialog named "Choose dates". - The calendar button is named "Choose dates", with the current range when there is one. - Every day in the range has `aria-selected`, so the span is announced, not only its ends. - A day of the month either side is decoration: hidden from assistive tech and not pickable, so each day is one button. - Presets are toggle buttons in a group named "Presets"; the one that matches the picked range is `aria-pressed`. - After both ends are in the field goes back to rest, as Date Picker's does after a pick.

) # File Uploader Choose files to send: drag them onto the drop zone or pick them with the button. It checks type, size and count, lists what was chosen, and shows progress or an error per file. It does not upload: your code does, and tells it how that is going. ## Variants | Mode | Use for | | --- | --- | | `multiple` | Attachments, a batch of photos: files are appended, up to `maxFiles`. | | Single | One document: an invoice, a CV. A new file replaces the chosen one, if it passes the checks. | Each file gets a type icon: a page with a coloured badge for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, image and audio, after Microsoft 365, from the extension or MIME type. Anything else is the bare page. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/file-uploader.json ``` - Source: [src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/inputs/FileUploader.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/file-uploader) - Behaviour: a native `` behind a kit [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Two more parts show only when needed: - **Errors**: one line per file that was not added, under the drop zone, e.g. "raw-scan.png is larger than 5 MB." - **File error**: in place of the progress ring, a short message from `getFileStatus`, e.g. "Upload failed". A long one truncates. ## Measurements One size. The buttons inside are `sm` Buttons, 24px tall. The uploader is 24rem wide unless `isFullWidth`. The type icon is 20px. ## Color The type badges keep fixed colours in both modes: they are each file type's identity, not the theme's, and white on each is above 4.5:1. The Choose button is an `accent contained` Button and the remove buttons `secondary ghost`; their states are Button's. ## States }, { label: 'Disabled', content: }, ]} > - **Dragging**: while a file is over the drop zone its edge turns solid `--ring` and it fills with `--accent`, so the change is not colour alone. - **Rejected or required and empty**: the drop zone's edge turns `--danger-text` and the errors list why, one line per file. - **Focus** is the Choose button's and the remove buttons' own ring. - **Uploading**: a progress ring beside the remove button while `progress` is under 100; it goes at 100. An `error` takes its place. - **Disabled** fades the icon and the buttons, not the text: none of it is a native label, so faded text would fail contrast rather than be exempt. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
### Design notes - **Checks on every path in.** The system picker filters by `accept`, but a drop, or "All files" in the picker, does not. The uploader checks the type, size and count of everything and says why a file was left out. - **A rejected file never replaces a good one.** In single-file mode a new file replaces the chosen one only if it passes the checks. - **The same file twice is one file.** Name, size and modified time match, so it is skipped rather than listed again. - **Uploading is yours.** Start it in `onFilesChange` and report through `getFileStatus`. ## When to use Use a File Uploader to attach files to a form: receipts to a claim, documents to an application. Say what is allowed in `helperText`, and set `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles` to match, so the rules are read before a file is turned away. } doCaption="The rules up front: types and size in the helper text, checked by accept and maxSize." dont={} dontCaption="No rules shown: people learn them one rejection at a time." /> Report upload progress per file with `getFileStatus`, and keep errors short ("Upload failed"): the row has room for a few words. ## When not to use - **For text people could paste.** Use a [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs). - **For a link to a file.** Use a [Text Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textinput--docs) with `type="url"`. ## Accessibility - Dragging is a shortcut, never the only way: the Choose button is a real button, reached by Tab, and opens the system picker. The file input itself is hidden from assistive tech so there is one control, not two. - The uploader is a `group` named by its label; `required` adds "(required)" to that name, since a group cannot be `aria-required`. Submitting it empty shows "Choose at least one file." (or "Choose a file.") in the errors and moves focus to the Choose button, instead of the browser's bubble on the hidden input. - The helper text and any errors describe the Choose button, so they are read when focus lands on it. - A polite status line announces "2 files added. 1 not added." and "report.pdf removed." - Remove buttons are named "Remove report.pdf". After a remove, focus moves to the next file's button, or back to Choose when the list is empty, so it is never lost. - The progress ring is a `progressbar` named "Uploading report.pdf", with its value. - While dragging, the drop zone's edge turns solid as well as changing colour.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { ProgressBar } from './ProgressBar' import * as ProgressBarStories from './ProgressBar.stories' # Progress Bar Shows how far a task with a known size has got: an upload, an install, the steps of a setup. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the fill, by meaning. The track is the same in all four. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `primary` | The default: a task the user started and is waiting on. | | `accent` | A strong fill in neutral black or white, where the brand colour would clash or already means something else. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: progress in the background, or one of many bars in a list. | | `destructive` | A task that is failing, or a quota about to run out. | `size` is the track's thickness, and `isRounded` gives it pill ends. When a task has started but its size is not known yet, go indeterminate, and switch to a value as soon as there is one. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/progress-bar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/ProgressBar.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/progress-bar) - Behaviour: [Base UI Progress](https://base-ui.com/react/components/progress) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy ## Measurements The bar fills the width of its container. Each size sets only the track's height. The value label is at least 4 characters wide, so the bar does not jump as the number grows from 9% to 100%. ## Color The fill is what carries the value, so it must clear 3:1 against the track. Not every accent's solid does (amber's is about 2.9:1 on white), so each variant fills with a colour meant to be read as text on the page, which keeps it at 3:1 or better on the track. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States A progress bar is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, { label: 'Complete', content: }, ]} > - **Progress** fills from the start edge, easing between values over `--duration-slow`. - **Indeterminate** slides a third of the track across, once every 1.4s. The value label is hidden: there is no value to show. - **Complete** is a full bar. It does not change on its own; replace or remove it when the task ends. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other prop goes to Base UI's `Progress.Root`: `id`, `aria-labelledby`, `min`, `format`, `locale`, `getAriaValueText`. ### Differences from the spec - **`max`, not `maxValue`**, the name Base UI and the native `` use. ## When to use Use a Progress Bar for a task that takes long enough to wait on and whose size is known, or will be: an upload, an import, the steps of a setup. Name the task in the `label`. } doCaption="The label names the task, so the reader knows what they are waiting for." dont={} dontCaption="A bare bar leaves sighted readers guessing what it measures, even with an aria-label." /> `value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage: Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers. Use it only where the context already says what the bar measures. ## When not to use - **For a short wait with no known size.** Use a [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs). - **For content whose shape you know.** A [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the layout. - **For steps the user moves through themselves.** Use a [Stepper](?path=/docs/components-navigation-stepper--docs): it names the steps, and the user can go back. ## Accessibility - `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0. - Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or `aria-label`. - The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both modes. The value label is `--muted-foreground`. - Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass. - A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Skeleton } from './Skeleton' import * as SkeletonStories from './Skeleton.stories' {/* On the page background: in dark mode --muted is the stage's own colour. */} export const card = { background: 'var(--background)', padding: 'var(--space-4)', borderRadius: 'var(--radius-lg)' } # Skeleton A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading, so the page keeps its layout and the reader sees what is coming. ## Variants `appearance` sets the corners, to match what the shape stands in for. Any appearance takes any size. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `circle` | An avatar or a round icon. Its height is its width. | | `square` | The default: an image, a media block, anything with square corners. | | `rounded` | Text, buttons and cards: anything with the kit's rounded corners. | `rows` stacks lines of text, the last one shorter so it reads as a paragraph rather than a block. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Skeleton } from 'zweihander/skeleton' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/skeleton.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Skeleton.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/skeleton](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/skeleton) - Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A skeleton is built from shapes like these, placed by the page in the layout of the content that will replace them. ## Measurements A skeleton has no sizes: `width` and `height` copy the content it stands in for. These are the defaults, and the parts it sizes itself. The default width is the container's. The last of several `rows` is 60% of the width. ## Color Every shape is one colour, the same subtle surface as a hover. It is below any contrast floor on purpose: a placeholder should read as "something goes here", not compete with content that has arrived. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the value follows. ## States A skeleton is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, ]} >
- **Static** is the default. - **Pulsing**, with `hasAnimation`, fades to 50% and back every 1.6s. It stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through to the outer element. ## When to use Use a Skeleton when you know the shape of what is loading: a list, a card, a profile. Match the shapes to the content that will replace them, with the same sizes and the same gaps. } doCaption="Shapes of the content that is coming: the layout holds when it arrives." dont={} dontCaption="One block for a whole card jumps to a different layout on load, which is worse than a spinner." /> Animate the few shapes that matter, or none: `hasAnimation` is off by default because a screen of pulsing shapes is noise. ## When not to use - **When you do not know the shape of what is coming.** Use a [Spinner](?path=/docs/components-loaders-spinner--docs). - **For a long task with a known size.** Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs). - **For a load that is usually instant.** A skeleton that flashes for 200ms is noise; show nothing, or a Spinner with a `delay`. ## Accessibility - **A skeleton is decoration** and is `aria-hidden`, with its `rows` hidden as one. It says nothing to a screen reader. - The region it stands in for has to say it is loading: put `aria-busy="true"` on it, as the CardPlaceholder story does, and remove it when the content arrives. - If the wait matters, announce it: a visually hidden status, or a Spinner with a label. - `--muted` is below 3:1 on the page in both modes, on purpose. It is not content, and should not compete with content that has arrived. - The pulse stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
