import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Spinner } from './Spinner' import * as SpinnerStories from './Spinner.stories' # Spinner Says that something is loading when there is no telling how long it will take, or, given a value, how far along it is. ## Variants `variant` is the colour of the indicator. The track and the label are the same in all three. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `accent` | The default: a quiet placeholder in `--foreground`, inside content that has its own colour. | | `primary` | A load the page is about, where the brand colour helps it be found: the first load of a view. | | `secondary` | Low emphasis: a spinner beside other muted text, or in a dense list. | With a `value` it stops spinning and becomes a progress ring, which reads better than a bar in a small space such as a thumbnail. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Spinner } from 'zweihander/spinner' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/spinner.json ``` - Source: [src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/loaders/Spinner.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/spinner](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/spinner) - Behaviour: a plain element; there is no behaviour here worth Base UI - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy While spinning, the indicator is a quarter of the ring turning once every `--duration-spin`. With no `label`, a visually hidden "Loading" stands in for it. ## Measurements The ring is an SVG drawn in a 24-unit box and scaled to the size, so the stroke (2.5 units) scales with it: 1.7px at `sm`, 3.3px at `lg`. ## Color The indicator is the part that has to be seen, so each variant takes a colour that clears 3:1 on the page. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States A spinner is not interactive: it has no hover, focus or pressed state. }, { label: 'Complete', content: }, ]} > - **Spinning** is the default, and what it shows with `isIndeterminate` even when given a `value`. - **Progress** fills the ring clockwise from twelve o'clock, easing between values over `--duration-slow`. - **Delayed**: with `delay`, nothing shows until it has passed. The live region is in the page, empty, from the start. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through to the outer element. ## When to use Use a Spinner when something is loading and you cannot say what its result will look like or how long it will take. Use one per region that is loading, labelled with what is coming. } doCaption="One spinner for the region, named for what is coming." dont={} dontCaption="A spinner per card says the same thing three times, and three screen-reader announcements." /> Give a load you expect to be fast a `delay` of 300–500ms. The spinner only appears if the wait turns out to be long enough to notice. ## When not to use - **When you know the shape of what is coming.** A [Skeleton](?path=/docs/components-loaders-skeleton--docs) keeps the layout and says more. - **For a long task with a known size**: an upload, an install. Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs), or a `value` here when space is tight. - **Inside a button.** Use the Button's `isLoading`: it keeps the button's width and focus and stops a second click. ## Accessibility - **Spinning, it is `role="status"`**, a polite live region, named by `label` or "Loading". The region renders empty and its text (the label, or a visually hidden "Loading") is inserted just after, or once `delay` has passed: screen readers announce text added to a live region that is already in the page, not a region that mounts full. - **With a value, it is `role="progressbar"`** with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin="0"` and `aria-valuemax="100"`. Values outside 0–100 are clamped. - The SVG is hidden. - The indicator clears 3:1 on the page in every variant: `--primary-text` (measured at 4.5:1 per accent), `--muted-foreground`, `--foreground`. The track is decoration and may be faint. - Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it slows to one turn in 2.5s rather than stopping, since a frozen arc reads as "stuck", and the progress ring stops easing between values. - Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove the spinner when the load ends, so the change is announced.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as BreadcrumbsStories from './Breadcrumbs.stories' # Breadcrumbs The trail from the top of a hierarchy down to the current page, each step a link back up. ## Variants Breadcrumbs has one look. What changes is the size, how a long trail collapses, and what sits between the steps. | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Under a page title, at body size. The default. | | `sm` | Dense headers, panels and side sheets, at `body-sm`. | | `maxItems` | Deep hierarchies, or a trail in a narrow place: the middle collapses to "…", which expands in place. | | `separator` | A slash or other glyph, where a chevron would clash with nearby icons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/breadcrumbs.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumbs.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/breadcrumbs) - Behaviour: a plain `
` and `
    `, after the [APG breadcrumb pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Each step is a list item: its link (or the ellipsis), then a separator. The last item has no separator after it. ## Measurements Breadcrumbs is text, not a row of controls: its height is the line height of its size. The separator icon is 1em: it follows the text size. ## Color One colour set. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States - **Hover** turns a link to `--foreground` and underlines it; on the ellipsis it fills an `--accent` chip. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the link or the ellipsis. - There is no disabled state: a level the reader cannot open is left out of the trail. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
    Every other `
    ` attribute passes through. ## When to use Use Breadcrumbs on pages three or more levels deep, under the page title, so a reader can see where they are and jump back up any number of levels. It is a secondary aid: the main navigation still has to get people everywhere. Keep the trail on one line. When it would wrap, collapse the middle with `maxItems`; the first level and the nearest ones stay in view. } doCaption="Collapse a long trail with maxItems: one line, and the levels that matter most stay visible." dont={} dontCaption="A trail that wraps reads as two rows and pushes the page down." /> Write each label as the title of the page it opens, short enough to scan. The last item is the current page, as text: a link to the page you are on does nothing useful. ## When not to use - **For history.** Breadcrumbs shows where a page sits, not how the reader got there. For "go back", use a Back link or [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). - **On a flat site.** One or two levels need no trail; the main navigation already says where you are. - **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper: it shows the steps ahead too, and which are done. - **As the main navigation.** Use a Nav Sidebar or Tabs. ## Accessibility - A `
    ` landmark named "Breadcrumb" (change it with `aria-label`), around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of items and the position of each. - Each level above the current page is a real ``, in the tab order. - The last item is text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link. - Separators are `aria-hidden`, so they are not read between items. - The ellipsis is a button named "Show 3 more". Enter or Space expands the trail and moves focus to the first item it revealed, rather than dropping it on the page. - The ellipsis is under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit area grows to 44×44px without it growing. - Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

variant.description: Colour. `accent` is the foreground, as on Button; `secondary` is muted, for footers and meta text.

size.description: Omit to inherit the surrounding text size, which is what a link inside a sentence wants.

underline.description: `always` inside running text: colour alone does not mark a link. `hover` only where the context already says "these are links", like a nav list.

isExternal.description: Opens in a new tab, with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, an external icon and "(opens in a new tab)" for screen readers.

isDisabled.description: Rendered without `href`, so it cannot navigate; `aria-disabled` says why.

render.description: Replaces the rendered element, e.g. a router's `<Link />`.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import { Link } from './Link' import * as LinkStories from './Link.stories' # Link Text that takes you somewhere: another page, a section of this one, an outside site. It navigates; it does not act. ## Variants `variant` is the colour; `underline` says whether the line shows at rest. Any variant takes either underline. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Primary | Links in running text and on their own. The default. | | Accent | Links in the foreground colour, where the brand colour would compete: dense lists, navigation. | | Secondary | Footers, captions and meta text, where the link is not the point. | | Underline | Use for | | --- | --- | | Always | Inside running text, where only the line tells a link from the words around it. The default. | | Hover | Places that are obviously lists of links: a nav list, a footer column. | Without a `size`, a link takes the size of the sentence around it, which is what a link in text wants. `sm`, `md` and `lg` are for links that stand alone. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Link } from 'zweihander/link' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/link.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Link.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Link.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/link](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/link) - Behaviour: a native ``; `render` from [Base UI useRender](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The underline is a text decoration on the link itself, 1px thick and offset 0.2em below the text. ## Measurements Each size sets only the text; without one, the link inherits it. The text is medium weight. The external icon is 0.9em, so it scales with the text, with 0.2em before it. ## Color The text and its underline share one colour. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. ## States }, ]} > - **Hover** thickens the underline from 1px to 2px and keeps the colour, so the link keeps the contrast it was measured at. With `underline="hover"`, hover is when the line appears. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the text. - **Disabled** is the enabled look at 50% opacity, with no `href`. - There is no visited style: most links in an app lead to screens, not documents, and a "seen it" colour there is noise. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `` attribute passes through, including `ref`, `target` and `rel`. ## When to use Use a Link to go somewhere: another page, a section of this one, a file, an outside site. Inside a sentence, keep the underline; let the link text say where it goes, so it still makes sense read on its own. } doCaption="The link text names the destination: it reads on its own, in a screen reader's list of links too." dont={} dontCaption={'"Click here" says nothing out of context, and hides where the link goes.'} /> Mark links that leave for another site with `isExternal` only when they open a new tab, and keep that rare: a new tab breaks the Back button. With a router, pass its link as `render`. Link merges its class and props onto it, and the router keeps control of navigation: ```tsx }>Settings ``` ## When not to use - **For an action.** Saving, deleting or opening a dialog is a [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs). A link-styled action looks like it will take you away, and does not respond to Space. - **For a prominent call to action that navigates.** Use a Button with `href`: it renders an `` with the weight of a button. - **For a trail of parent pages.** Use Breadcrumbs. - **For moving through pages of a list.** Use Pagination. ## Accessibility - A real ``, so it is in the tab order, opens with Enter, and shows up in a screen reader's list of links. - Underlined by default: colour alone does not mark a link for someone who cannot tell the colours apart (WCAG 1.4.1). - `isExternal` adds "(opens in a new tab)" to the accessible name, and sets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`: a new tab that opens without warning strands people who cannot see it happen. - `isDisabled` removes `href`, the only thing that stops an `` navigating, drops the click handlers and sets `aria-disabled`. Without an `href` it leaves the tab order. Prefer hiding a link that cannot be followed, or saying in text why it is unavailable. - Every variant is a text colour measured at 4.5:1 on the page, and hover does not change it. - Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, 2px offset.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as MenuStories from './Menu.stories' # Menu A list of actions that opens from a button: the "…" on a row, an "Actions" dropdown, a "View" menu of toggles. It acts or toggles; to pick a value for a form, use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs). ## Variants Menu has one look. What changes is the kind of entry in `items`, and a menu can mix them: | Entry | Use for | | --- | --- | | Action (the default) | Something to do now: Edit, Duplicate, Delete. Closes the menu. `isDestructive` draws it in the danger colour. | | Link (`href`) | Going somewhere: Documentation, Settings. A real ``. | | Submenu (`items`) | A set of choices that belongs under one item: Move to, Share with. | | Checkbox (`type: 'checkbox'`) | Settings that are on or off, several at a time: Show hidden files. Keeps the menu open. | | Radio (`type: 'radio'`) | One of a few settings: Sort by name, date or size. Keeps the menu open. | | Group (`type: 'group'`) and separator | Structure for a longer menu: a label over related items, a rule between sets. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/menu.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Menu.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/menu](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/menu) - Behaviour: [Base UI Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy A link item has the same parts as an action. Checkbox and radio items show a check where an action shows its icon, so their labels line up. ## Measurements The popup is the Select list's surface. Each item is a row of the md control tier, with the normal pad: its text is left-aligned. The item's corner nests inside the popup's: the popup radius minus the popup padding, so the highlight runs parallel to the popup edge. The popup is at least 12rem wide, or the trigger's width if that is wider, and no taller than the space on screen: past that it scrolls. It opens 4px from the trigger. ## Color The destructive item uses the danger text colour, not the solid: it reads at 4.5:1 on the popup and on its highlight. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Highlighted** is where the arrow keys or the pointer are: a `--accent` fill, the icon taking the text colour. A submenu's item stays highlighted while its submenu is open. Focus moves with the highlight, so there is no separate focus ring inside the popup. - **Disabled** items are muted at 60% opacity and skipped by the arrow keys (Archive, above). - **Checked** checkbox and radio items show the check; unchecked ones keep the empty column. - The trigger's own hover, focus and pressed states are the [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs)'s. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`items` is data, like Select's `options`, not child components. `shortcut` is display only: binding the key is left to the page, which knows what else is bound. ## When to use Use a Menu for actions that belong to one thing but would crowd the screen as buttons: the actions on a table row, a card's overflow, a toolbar's "More". Keep it short, put the most used item first, and give destructive actions the last place, after a separator. } doCaption="Delete last, after a separator, in the danger colour." dont={} dontCaption="Delete between two everyday actions: one arrow key too far and it is chosen." /> } doCaption="A menu of actions. Each item does something now." dont={} dontCaption="A menu standing in for a form field. Use a Select: it has a label, a value and a form name." /> ## When not to use - **To pick a value for a form.** Use a [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs), or a [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs) when the list is long enough to search. - **For one or two actions.** Show them as [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): a hidden action is one fewer person finds. - **For the app's main navigation.** Use a [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) or [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs), which show where the reader is. - **For content: a form, a preview.** Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). A menu holds only menu items. ## Accessibility - The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the popup is a `role="menu"` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio`, with `aria-checked` on the toggles and `aria-disabled` on disabled items. - Keyboard: Enter, Space or Arrow Down on the trigger opens it; arrows move (disabled items are skipped), typing a few letters jumps to the matching item, Enter selects, Arrow Right opens a submenu and Arrow Left closes it, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. - Toggles keep the menu open, so several can be changed in one go; actions close it and focus returns to the trigger. - The icon and shortcut are hidden from assistive tech; the label names the item. Give `textValue` when a label is not plain text, or typeahead cannot find it. - A disabled link has no `href`, so it cannot be followed. - Items are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - `isModal` (the default) makes the rest of the page inert while the menu is open, so a screen reader stays in the menu.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PaginationStories from './Pagination.stories' # Pagination Moves through a long list one page at a time: previous, next, and the page numbers around the current one. ## Variants Pagination has one look. What changes is the size, how many numbers show, and whether the pages are buttons or links. | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `md` | Under a table or a list of results. The default. | | `sm` | Dense places: a card, a side panel, a compact table footer. | | `getHref` | Pages with their own URL: each page is a link that can be opened in a new tab and shared. | | Buttons | Pages that only exist in this view's state, such as a filtered list in a dialog. The default. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/pagination.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Pagination.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/pagination](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/pagination) - Behaviour: a plain `
` around a list of buttons or links - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The first and last page always show, the current page keeps a sibling each side, and "…" appears only where it hides two or more pages. A single hidden page is shown instead, since "…" would take the same room. So the number of controls stays the same as you move through the middle, and Next does not jump. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A control is square at its minimum; the inline padding only shows on a page number of three digits or more. Previous and next have no padding, so they stay square. ## Color One colour set: the current page is the only fill. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. At rest a control has no fill. ## States - **Selected**: the current page is filled with `--primary`, medium weight. It does not change on hover, and pressing it does nothing. - **Hover** fills a page, Previous or Next with an `--accent` chip. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, 2px outside the control. - **Disabled**: Previous on the first page (above) and Next on the last, at 50% opacity. As buttons they are `disabled`; as links they lose their `href`. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through. `paginationItems(page, total, siblings, boundary)` is exported too, for building your own. ## When to use Use Pagination under a long list or table when the reader needs to know where they are in it and jump to a page: search results, an audit log, an order history. Put it below the content it pages, and keep the list's position stable as pages change. Leave `siblingCount` and `boundaryCount` at 1. The control stays short and keeps the same width as the reader moves, so Next stays under the pointer. } doCaption="The default range: first, last, and the current page with a neighbour each side, on one line." dont={} dontCaption="Every page number at once wraps over several lines and buries the current page." /> When the pages have URLs, pass `getHref`, so a page can be opened in a new tab, bookmarked and shared. ## When not to use - **For a feed read top to bottom.** Load more as the reader scrolls, or with a "Load more" [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs): page numbers mean nothing in a stream. - **For a few items.** If everything fits on one page, show it all. - **For the steps of a task.** Use a Stepper. - **For switching between views of one thing.** Use Tabs. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Pagination", around a list. - Each page control is named "Page 3"; the current one has `aria-current="page"`. Previous and next are named "Previous page" and "Next page". - At either end, Previous or Next is disabled. The label sits under its marker, so every step gets the same width whatever its label. | | Vertical | Steps with long descriptions, or a narrow column beside the form. | | `sm` | Dense places: a dialog, a side panel. | | Navigable (`onStepClick`) | Flows where going back to fix an earlier step is normal. Finished steps become buttons. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/stepper.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Stepper.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/stepper](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/stepper) - Behaviour: a plain `

Horizontal, a connector runs along the markers' centre line from one marker to the next, `--space-2` clear of each. ## Color Complete and current share the primary colour: the filled disc says done, the ring says here. The current ring uses `--primary-text`, the step of the accent that reads at 4.5:1 on the page, because it frames a number. ## States A step's status is its state. Every other `
` attribute passes through. A step's `status` is only for the exception, such as an error: the rest is worked out from `current`. Only finished steps can be clicked; upcoming ones stay text, because a flow that can be skipped ahead is a set of Tabs. ## When to use Use a Stepper when a task is split into a few steps that must be done in order, and it helps to know how many are left: checkout, onboarding, an import wizard. Keep it to three to five steps with a word or two each. } doCaption="Four steps, one word each: the whole flow at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Ten steps squeeze every label and make the flow look longer than it is. Merge steps, or drop the stepper." /> ## When not to use - **For sections the reader can visit in any order.** Use [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs). - **For progress with no steps to name**, such as an upload. Use a [Progress Bar](?path=/docs/components-loaders-progressbar--docs). - **For a single-page form.** Headings do the job; a stepper over one page promises steps that are not there. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Progress" around an ordered list: screen readers announce the number of steps and the position of each. - The current step has `aria-current="step"`. - The marker is decorative, so each label carries its status in visually hidden text: "Account, completed", "Invite, not started", "Workspace, has an error". - Without `onStepClick` nothing is focusable. import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TabsStories from './Tabs.stories' # Tabs Switches between views of the same thing without leaving the page: Overview, Activity, Settings of one project. ## Variants `appearance` is the look. Either takes either size and orientation. | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `underline` | The sections of a page or a panel. Tabs sit on a 1px rule; a bar slides under the selected one. The default. | | `pills` | A compact view switch in a toolbar, such as List / Board. A segmented track with the selected tab lifted. | | Form | Use for | | --- | --- | | `isFullWidth` | Two to four tabs that should fill a narrow container, such as a side panel or a phone screen. | | `vertical` | Many sections, or labels too long for a row: settings pages, a panel beside its content. | | Icons | Recognisable icons beside the label. Never an icon alone: the label is the tab's name. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tabs } from 'zweihander/tabs' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tabs.json ``` - Source: [src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/navigation/Tabs.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tabs](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tabs) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The indicator is one element for the whole list. It moves to the selected tab rather than each tab drawing its own, so a change of tab slides it across. ## Measurements Each size is a control tier (Foundations / Sizing). A tab is a button in a row, so it takes the spacious inline padding. The underline indicator is 2px. In `pills`, the track has a 2px inset and the chip's corner is the track's minus 2px, so the two stay concentric at every size. ## Color Each appearance has its own label colours and indicator. Switch the theme and the accent in the toolbar: the values follow. Pill labels use `--subtle-foreground`, not `--muted-foreground`: that is 4.3:1 on the `--muted` track, under 4.5:1. ## States - **Selected**: the label takes the selected colour and the indicator slides under it (`underline`) or behind it (`pills`). - **Hover** brings an unselected label up to `--foreground`. It adds no fill. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn just inside the tab, so it is not clipped by the list. - **Disabled** (Archive, above) is the enabled look at 50% opacity. It still takes focus. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use Tabs to split one thing into views the reader moves between freely, in any order: the overview, activity and settings of a project. Every panel is about the same object, and only one is needed at a time. Label each tab with a word or two. Labels do not wrap or shrink, so long ones push the row past its container. } doCaption="Short labels, a word or two: the row fits, and each reads at a glance." dont={} dontCaption="Long labels run past the edge of the container. Shorten them, or go vertical." /> Use `underline` for the sections of a page and `pills` for a view switch in a toolbar. Name the tab list with `aria-label` when no heading does. Selection is manual by default: arrow keys move focus, Enter or Space selects, so a slow panel does not load on every keypress. Turn on `activateOnFocus` only for light panels. ## When not to use - **For a sequence.** Steps that must be done in order belong in a Stepper. - **To compare content side by side.** Tabs show one panel at a time; put things that are read together on the same view. - **To go to another page.** Use links, a Nav Sidebar or Breadcrumbs: a tab changes the view, not the URL. - **For one setting with two or three options.** Use a radio group or a [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) group: that changes a value, not the view. ## Accessibility - `role="tablist"` of `role="tab"` buttons with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a `role="tabpanel"` labelled by its tab. - One tab stop: Tab moves into the list on the selected tab and the next Tab moves on to the panel. - Arrow keys move between tabs (Left and Right, or Up and Down when vertical, with `aria-orientation` set); Home and End jump to the ends. - Arrows move focus without selecting; Enter or Space selects. With `activateOnFocus`, arrows select as they go. - A disabled tab still takes focus, marked `aria-disabled`, so it is found and announced, but it cannot be selected. - Tabs are 24 or 32px tall and grow to 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`). - Focus ring: 2px `--ring`, drawn inside the tab.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as AlertStories from './Alert.stories' # Alert A message about a page or a section that stays until the situation changes or the reader dismisses it: something went wrong, needs attention, or worked. ## Variants `variant` is the colour, by meaning; `appearance` is the emphasis. Any variant takes any appearance. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `info` | Something worth knowing that changes nothing: a plan change, scheduled maintenance. | | `success` | Something finished and stays true: a domain verified, an import done. | | `warning` | Something that will go wrong if nobody acts: a card expiring, a quota nearly used. | | `danger` | Something that went wrong and needs a next step: a failed upload, a lost connection. | | Appearance | Use for | | --- | --- | | `subtle` | The default. Sits on the page without shouting. | | `outlined` | On a tinted or busy background, where a tint would disappear. | | `solid` | The one message nobody should miss, such as an outage banner. Rarely more than one per page. | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/alert.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Alert.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/alert](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/alert) - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the description is required. The icon is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. The text is body text, so an alert sits in running content without a jump in size. The border is always there, 1px and transparent unless `outlined`, so switching appearance never moves the content. ## Color Each variant reads four tokens, the same four as a Tag of that variant, so the two always agree. Subtle and outlined keep the description in `--foreground`: a paragraph in the variant's colour is tiring to read, so the colour goes on the icon and the title. ## States The alert itself has no states. Its close button does. - **Hover** tints the close button with 15% of the alert's own text colour, so it reads on every variant and appearance. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline, inside the button's edge. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ### Differences from the spec - **Placed in the content, not at the top of the screen.** The spec describes a prominent message at the top; here an alert goes where the thing it is about is. An outage banner is a `solid` alert placed at the top by the page. - **Closing is the parent's job.** `onClose` reports the click and the alert stays until whoever rendered it removes it, so "dismissed" lives in your state and can be remembered across visits. ## When to use Use an Alert for a message about a page or a section that should stay put until it is dealt with: a failed save, a card about to expire, an import that finished. The title says what happened; the description says what it means and what to do. } doCaption="Say what happened and offer the next step." dont={} dontCaption="“Something went wrong” leaves the red box to do the talking, and the reader with nothing to do." /> The icon is decorative, so the variant has to be clear from the words too: "Upload failed", not just a red box. ## When not to use - **For news about something that just happened and needs nothing more.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs): it goes away by itself. - **For a one-line message under a form or a group of fields.** Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs). - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a decision the reader must make before going on.** Use a Modal. ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default: an alert on the page when it loads is read in order, like the text around it, and does not interrupt. - An alert that **appears** in response to something (a failed save) needs `isLive`. `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once; `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait for the screen reader to finish. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The close button is a native `

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as InlineAlertStories from './InlineAlert.stories' # Inline Alert A one-line message in the flow of a form or a section, with no box, no title and no close button: "Changes are saved automatically", "Couldn't reach the server". ## Variants `variant` is the colour, by meaning, and the whole line takes it. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `info` | A fact about what is above it: "Changes are saved automatically." | | `success` | A check that passed: "Domain verified." | | `warning` | A consequence to know before going on: "This link expires in 24 hours." | | `danger` | Something that failed: "Couldn't reach the server." | ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { InlineAlert } from 'zweihander/inline-alert' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/inline-alert.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/InlineAlert.tsx) - Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The icon box is one line tall, so on a message that wraps it stays on the first line. ## Measurements No padding, border or background: it lines up with the text and fields around it. ## Color The whole line, icon and message, takes the variant's text colour. An Alert can keep its message in `--foreground` because its box carries the colour; an inline alert has no box, so the text does. Every `--*-text` token is 4.5:1 on the page in both modes, so a message of any length stays readable. The action keeps its own colours: a Link or a Button, as passed. ## States The message has no states. An action in it has its own. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Inline Alert for a short message about the thing right above it: a group of fields, a whole form, a section. A failed submit is the common case. } doCaption="An error about one field goes on the field, as its helper text: it is read when the field is focused." dont={} dontCaption="An inline alert under a field is not tied to it: a screen reader in the field never hears it." /> ## When not to use - **For an error on one field.** Use the field's own `validationState` and `helperText`, tied to it with `aria-describedby`. - **For a message about a whole page or region**, or one that needs a title, an action row or a close button. Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs). - **For news about something that just happened.** Use a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs). ## Accessibility - A plain `
` by default, read in order with the page. - `isLive` for a message that appears in response to something (a failed submit): `danger` and `warning` become `role="alert"` and are read at once, `info` and `success` become `role="status"` and wait. - The icon is `aria-hidden`: the words carry the meaning. - The action is whatever you pass (a Link, a Button) and keeps its own keyboard behaviour and focus ring.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ToastStories from './Toast.stories' # Toast A short message in a corner of the screen about something that just happened: saved, sent, moved, failed. It closes itself after a few seconds and never blocks the page. Try it: the toast opens in the corner of this window. ## Variants `variant` colours the icon only; the message stays in the surface's text colour. | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | `default` | Most toasts: something done, nothing to judge. "File moved to Trash." | | `info` | A neutral fact about what just happened: "Sync paused while offline." | | `success` | A result worth confirming because it was not obvious: "Invite sent to 12 people." | | `warning` | Done, with a catch: "Saved, but 2 rows were skipped." | | `danger` | Something failed. Interrupts the screen reader. Say what to do next, and keep the way to do it on the page too. | `promise()` adds a loading toast that becomes `success` or `danger` when the promise settles. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { ToastProvider, useToast } from 'zweihander/toast' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/toast.json ``` - Source: [src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/notifications/Toast.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/toast](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/toast) - Behaviour: [Base UI Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the title, or the description alone, is required. The icon box is one line of body text tall, so it sits on the title's line. ## Measurements One size. Toasts stack with a gap, the newest nearest the edge they grow from. At most 24rem wide, and never wider than the window less the edge distance on both sides. ## Color The surface takes the opposite appearance to the page: dark toasts on a light page, light on a dark one. The contrast pulls the eye to a message that is only there for a few seconds. The tokens below are read in that opposite appearance. `default` shows no icon. ## States }, ]} > - **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`. Hovering the stack also pauses every toast's timer. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline inside the action or the close button. Focus in the stack pauses the timers too. - **Pending** is a `promise()` toast: a spinner in place of the icon, and no timer until it settles. - **Entering** fades in and slides `--space-2` from the edge the stack grows from; **leaving** fades out. With reduced motion, only the fade. ## API `ToastProvider` wraps the app once: {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`useToast()`, anywhere inside it, shows and closes toasts: ```tsx const toast = useToast() toast.add({ title: 'File moved to Trash', action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: restore } }) ``` {/* Markdown tables do not scroll by themselves on a phone either. */}
| `useToast()` | | | --- | --- | | `add(options)` | Shows a toast, returns its id. | | `update(id, options)` | Changes one in place; only the options given change. | | `close(id?)` | Closes one, or all. | | `promise(promise, { loading, success, error })` | A loading toast that becomes success or danger when the promise settles. | | Option | Values | | | --- | --- | --- | | `title`, `description` | node | | | `variant` | `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` | `default` | | `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | One button. | | `timeout` | number (ms) | The provider's by default. `0` keeps it until dismissed. | | `priority` | `low`, `high` | `high` by default for `danger`. | | `onClose` | function | |
### Differences from the spec - **Bottom right by default**, where the spec suggests top right. `placement` takes any corner or edge centre. ## When to use Use a Toast to confirm something the reader just did, when the result is not already visible: moved, sent, copied, saved in the background. Offer "Undo" when it can be undone. } doCaption="News about something just done, with a way to undo it. Undo is also reachable from the Trash." dont={} dontCaption="A problem the reader has to fix goes away in a few seconds. Put it in an Alert on the page." /> Keep it to a few words. A toast is read in passing, often half-noticed. ## When not to use - **For something the reader must act on, or might need to read twice.** Use an [Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-alert--docs) on the page, or a Modal for a decision. - **For an error in a form.** Use the field's own error, or an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) under the form. - **As the only way to an action.** The toast goes away; the same action ("Undo") must be reachable somewhere else. - **To confirm what is already visible.** A row that appears in a table needs no "Row added" toast. ## Accessibility - The stack is a polite live region: a new toast is announced without interrupting. `danger` toasts (and any with `priority: 'high'`) are `role="alertdialog"` and announced at once. - Each toast is a non-modal dialog named by its title, or by its description when it has none (as `promise()` toasts do). - Timers pause while the pointer is over the stack or focus is in it, so there is time to reach the action. F6 moves focus to the stack. - The close button is named `Dismiss`; Enter and Space press it. On touch screens its hit area grows to 44×44px, and a toast swipes away toward the nearest edge. - A toast raised from inside a modal shows above it and is not hidden from assistive tech by it.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as ModalStories from './Modal.stories' # Modal A dialog over the page that has to be dealt with before going back: a short form, a confirmation, a decision. Everything behind it is dimmed and out of reach until it closes. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Dialog (default) | A short task on its own: edit a profile, invite people. A close button, Escape and a press on the backdrop all close it. | | Alert (`isAlert`) | A decision with consequences: delete, discard, leave. No close button and a press on the backdrop does nothing, so it ends only through its own buttons or Escape. | `size` sets the maximum width: `sm` (24rem) for an alert, `md` (32rem) for a short form, `lg` (48rem) for long content. Taller than the screen, the body scrolls and the title and footer stay in view. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Modal, ModalClose } from 'zweihander/modal' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/modal.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Modal.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/modal](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/modal) - Behaviour: [Base UI Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog) and [Alert Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open modals on this tab and the next are pictures: real modals rendered in a frame with `container`, not modal (`isModal={false}`) and inert, so they do not lock this page or take its focus. ## Measurements Width is `size`: at most 24rem (`sm`), 32rem (`md`) or 48rem (`lg`), and never wider than the screen less its margin. The border is 1px. Backdrop and modal sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-base`. ## Color Buttons in the footer keep their own colours: see Button. ## States The modal is open or closed. Opening fades the backdrop in and scales the container up from 97%; closing reverses it. The close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the button with `--accent`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button, so it is not clipped at the container's corner. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`ModalClose` closes the modal it is in. Give it your own button with `render`: `}>Cancel`. ## When to use Reach for a modal last: it stops everything else. Use one when the task must be finished or abandoned before going on, or for a decision with consequences. For a decision, use `isAlert`, say exactly what will happen in the description, and name the buttons after what they do. } doCaption="Name the buttons after what they do: Delete, Keep project. The choice reads without the question." dont={} dontCaption="OK and Cancel make the reader go back to the question to know which one deletes." /> Put the main action last in the footer, and dismiss actions (Cancel, Keep) in the `secondary` variant. ## When not to use - **For a small form tied to one button**, such as Share or a filter. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs): it opens beside the button and leaves the page usable. - **For information**: a success, a warning, a tip. Use an [Inline Alert](?path=/docs/components-notifications-inlinealert--docs) or a [Toast](?path=/docs/components-notifications-toast--docs); neither stops the reader. - **For a long or many-step task.** Give it a page of its own. - **Over another modal.** Close the first, or move the second step into it. ## Accessibility - `role="dialog"` (or `alertdialog`), named by the title and described by the description. - Opening moves focus to the first focusable element, or `initialFocus`, and traps it inside. The page behind is `aria-hidden`, its pointer events are blocked by the backdrop, and its scroll is locked. Closing returns focus to the trigger. - `isModal={false}` drops the focus trap, the scroll lock and the hidden page, but the backdrop still covers the page. It is for pictures of a modal, such as the ones on these tabs: a real modal stays modal. - Escape closes it, as does a press outside unless `isAlert` or `closeOnBackdropClick={false}`. An alert dialog closes only through its own buttons (and Escape). - **One layer with the popups.** Modal, Popover, Select and Combobox all sit at `--layer-overlay`. Each portals to the end of `` when it opens, so the most recent is on top: a Select opened inside a modal lists its options above the modal, which a higher modal layer would hide. - The close button is named `Close` (`closeLabel`), has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

components-overlays-popover--docs.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as PopoverStories from './Popover.stories' # Popover A small panel anchored to a button, for content you interact with: a share form, a filter, a set of options. It opens on click and stays until you close it. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Non-modal (default) | Most popovers. Tab can leave it and the page stays usable while it is open. | | Modal (`isModal`) | A popover that must be finished or closed first: focus stays inside, the page does not scroll and presses outside are blocked. | | `openOnHover` | A preview that also opens on hover. Click, keyboard and touch still open it. | A title is optional. Without one, name the popover with `aria-label`: ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/popover.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Popover.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/popover](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/popover) - Behaviour: [Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open popovers on this tab and the next are pictures: real popovers rendered in place with `container` and inert, the popup laid out under the trigger where it opens. ## Measurements The container is as wide as its content, at most 22rem and never wider than the room beside the trigger. It has no arrow: it opens 6px from the trigger and lines up with it, which already ties the two. It has a 1px border and a semibold title. The close button is 20px: 2px around its icon, one line of text tall. Popovers sit on the `--layer-overlay` layer and fade in over `--duration-fast`. ## Color Select and Combobox lists use the same surface: `--popover`, its border and shadow. ## States The popover is open or closed. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 97%, from the trigger's side. The trigger keeps the states of its own component (see Button); the close button is the only part with states of its own: - **Hover** fills the close button with `--accent`. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the button. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
## When to use Use a Popover for a short task that belongs to the button that opens it: share a file, set a filter, pick from a few options. It holds links, inputs and buttons, which a Tooltip must not. } doCaption="A short task tied to its button: one field and one action." dont={} dontCaption="A whole form in a popover. It closes on a stray press outside and loses the work: use a Modal." /> ## When not to use - **For a label or a hint** on hover or focus. Use a [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs). - **For a list of actions or commands.** Use a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs): it has the arrow-key navigation a list of commands needs. - **For a long form or a decision with consequences.** Use a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs). ## Accessibility - The popup is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or `aria-label`) and described by `description`. The trigger carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`. - Opening moves focus into the popup; Escape or a press outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger. - **Non-modal by default:** Tab can leave the popup, and the page stays usable. `isModal` switches to Base UI's modal mode: focus is trapped, page scroll is locked and presses outside are blocked. - Base UI only traps focus when the popup contains a close button, and a touch screen reader needs one to get out. So a modal popover without `hasCloseButton` still renders one: hidden until it has keyboard focus, then shown in the corner, so focus is never invisible. - `openOnHover` adds hover to click, it does not replace it: the content stays reachable by keyboard and touch. - The close button has the 2px focus ring and a 44px hit area on touch screens.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as TooltipStories from './Tooltip.stories' # Tooltip A short label that appears when you hover over or focus a control: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, a one-line hint. ## Variants There is one tooltip. It opens on hover after a short delay and on keyboard focus at once. Wrap a row of tooltips in `TooltipGroup` so that once one has opened, moving to the next opens it without the delay: Only one tooltip is open at a time: opening one closes any other. Hover or focus the triggers above to see them. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { Tooltip, TooltipGroup } from 'zweihander/tooltip' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tooltip.json ``` - Source: [src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/overlays/Tooltip.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/tooltip](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/tooltip) - Behaviour: [Base UI Tooltip](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy The open tooltips on this tab and the next are pictures: real tooltips held open and rendered in place with `container`, laid out above the trigger where they open. ## Measurements The container is as wide as its text, at most 20rem and never wider than the room beside the trigger; longer text wraps. It opens 6px from the trigger, on the `--layer-tooltip` layer, above popovers and modals, so a tooltip on a control inside one still shows. It fades in over `--duration-fast`. ## Color Inverted in both modes: a tooltip is not part of the page, and the dark-on-light (light-on-dark in dark mode) box says so, at the same contrast as body text. ## States }, { label: 'Open', content: }, ]} /> - **Closed** until the pointer rests on the trigger for `delay` (300ms), or the trigger takes keyboard focus, which opens it at once. - **Open** until Escape, blur or the pointer leaves, after `closeDelay`. Opening fades it in and scales it up from 96%. - The trigger keeps the states of its own component; the tooltip has none of its own. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
`TooltipGroup` is Base UI's `Tooltip.Provider`: tooltips inside it share one delay. ## When to use Use a Tooltip for a label or a hint: the name of an icon-only button, a keyboard shortcut, one line on what a control does. 300ms before it opens is quick enough to feel responsive and long enough that tooltips do not flash as the pointer crosses a toolbar. } doCaption="A short label that repeats the icon-only button's name for sighted users." dont={} dontCaption="Rules the reader needs to fill the field. Touch cannot open a tooltip, and it hides as soon as focus moves on: put the rules under the field." /> ## When not to use - **For anything a reader needs to finish a task.** Put it on the page: a tooltip cannot be reached by touch, and it disappears the moment you look away. - **For links, buttons or other interactive content.** Hover and touch cannot reach the tooltip. Use a [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs). - **On a disabled button.** It is not focusable, so its tooltip never opens by keyboard. Put the reason it is disabled in text next to it. ## Accessibility - It opens on hover after `delay` and on keyboard focus at once, and closes on Escape, blur or pointer leave. - Base UI keeps tooltips out of the accessibility tree. This component gives the popup `role="tooltip"` and, while it is open, points the trigger's `aria-describedby` at it, so it is read as a description. - It is a **description, not a name.** An icon-only button still needs its own `aria-label`; the tooltip then shows that label to sighted users too. - The trigger must be focusable: a Button, a link, a field. - `--background` on `--foreground` reads at 16:1 or more in both modes.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as EmptyStateStories from './EmptyState.stories' # Empty State What a list, a table or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet: why it is empty, and what to do about it. ## Variants There are three kinds of empty, and they need three kinds of copy. The component is the same; the words and the action are not. | Kind | Use for | | --- | --- | | First use | Nothing has been made yet. Say what will live here, and offer the way in: "No projects yet", New project. | | No results | A search or a filter matched nothing. Say what was searched, and offer to clear it: "No projects match", Clear search. | | Cleared out | Everything is done. Often no action at all: "All caught up". | `size="sm"` fits a panel or a table body; `md` fills a page or a section. ## Resources From npm, or copied into your project through the registry: ```js import { EmptyState } from 'zweihander/empty-state' ``` ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/empty-state.json ``` - Source: [src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/states/EmptyState.tsx) - Spec: [uiguideline.com/components/empty-state](https://www.uiguideline.com/components/empty-state) - Behaviour: a plain element, no Base UI part - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy Only the title is required. [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs) and [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs) are this layout with the disc in their own tone. ## Measurements The icon is half the disc's size. The description wraps at 40 characters (`max-inline-size: 40ch`), so it stays a short paragraph on a wide page. ## Color One tone: neutral. Switch the theme in the toolbar: the values follow. The container has no fill: it takes the surface it sits on. ## States Empty State itself is static: it has no hover, focus or pressed look. Its action does, and those are the action's own (here, an outlined Button). ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through, including `ref`. ## When to use Use an Empty State wherever a list, a table or a page can have nothing in it: before the first item is made, after a search matches nothing, when everything is done. Write the title for the reader's situation, and give them the next step. } doCaption="Say what is empty and what will live here, and offer the way in." dont={} dontCaption="“No data” says neither why nor what to do next." /> ## When not to use - **When loading failed.** Use an [Error State](?path=/docs/components-states-errorstate--docs): "No projects" when the request failed tells the reader their work is gone. - **When a flow has finished.** Use a [Success State](?path=/docs/components-states-successstate--docs). - **While content is loading.** Use a Skeleton or a Spinner: an empty state shown before the data arrives flashes the wrong message. ## Accessibility - The title is a real heading, so a screen reader user jumping by headings finds out the area is empty. Set `headingLevel` to fit the outline: `3` inside a section headed by an `h2`. - The icon is `aria-hidden`; the title has to say it all. - It is not a live region, so it is not announced when it replaces results. If a search updates as you type, announce the count elsewhere, in a `role="status"` line such as "0 results".

# App Content

The page region of an app: the `main` landmark. One of the three pieces
the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places;
the shell puts it around its children, so you rarely render it yourself.
It reads the shell's grid and canvas, so it is not used on its own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/app-content.json
```

## Flat

The Theme's `contentStyle="flat"` (the default): one card surface, inset
8px from the shell's edges at every density. Blocks inside are
[Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) with
`appearance="surface"`, which become sections ruled off at the top.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.Flat} />

## On the canvas

`contentStyle="card"`: no surface; the page sits on the canvas and each
surface Card is raised.

<Canvas of={AppContentStories.OnCanvas} />

## Props

Any `main` attribute; the App Shell passes the `id` its skip link targets.

## Layout

- Below 48rem the flat surface drops its inset, edge and rounding and goes
  flush.
- The page padding is `--space-container`, `--space-section` from 64rem.
- Only the page scrolls; the shell's other pieces stay put.
- The surface restates `--background` as `--card` (flat) or as the
  canvas's solid colour (card), so components that draw "the surface under
  me" match it.

## Accessibility

- The `main` landmark, focusable (`tabIndex={-1}`) so the shell's skip
  link can move focus to it.
- On a canvas, text takes the canvas text colours (the Theme's
  `canvas-foreground` and `canvas-muted-foreground` tokens); the kit checks
  them for its own canvases.

patterns-application-ui-data-table-page-.content:
import { Meta, Canvas } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DataTablePageStories from './DataTablePage.stories'

<Meta of={DataTablePageStories} />

# Data Table Page

A list screen: search and filters above a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs),
what is shown and the pages below it, and, while rows are selected, what
you can do with them. Two pieces, `TableToolbar` (with
`TableToolbarGroup`) and `TableFooter`, around the kit's Table, Search,
Select and Pagination. Filtering, paging and the data are yours: the
stories show one way to wire them.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/data-table-page.json
```

## Toolbar and pagination

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.ToolbarAndPagination} />

## Bulk actions

With `selectedCount` above zero the toolbar swaps its tools for the
selection's actions and a "Clear selection" button, on the accent
surface so the change of mode is visible.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.BulkActions} />

## Empty result

When nothing matches, the Table's `emptyState` says so and offers the way
back; the footer goes away.

<Canvas of={DataTablePageStories.EmptyResult} />

## Props

**TableToolbar**

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | node | – | Search, filters, the primary action. |
| `selectedCount` | number | `0` | From 1, the selection bar replaces the children. |
| `selectionActions` | node | – | |
| `onClearSelection` | function | – | Shows "Clear selection". |
| `selectionLabel` | `(n) => string` | `"{n} selected"` | |

`TableToolbarGroup` wraps the part that should take the free space and
wrap first, usually the search and filters.

**TableFooter** takes `summary` ("Showing 1–5 of 12") and, as children,
usually a Pagination.

## Behaviour to copy

- **Filtering returns to page 1.** A new query on page 3 would otherwise
  show an empty page, or a page the reader never asked for.
- **Selection is by id**, so it survives sorting and paging (Table's
  `getRowId`), and an action clears it once it has been applied.

## Layout

- No breakpoints: both bars are flex rows that wrap, so they adapt to the
  width of their container, not the viewport.
- `TableToolbarGroup` grows from 16rem and wraps first. On a phone the
  search takes its own line and the filters and the primary action flow
  under it, instead of anything shrinking below use.
- In selection mode the actions are pushed to the end of the bar and drop
  under the count when they no longer fit.
- The footer puts the summary at the start and the pagination at the end;
  when both do not fit, the pagination wraps under the summary.

## Accessibility

- The selection count is a polite status line that is always in the page,
  so "2 selected" is announced as it changes, and silence when it clears.
- Search and the status filter are named ("Search projects", "Status")
  without visible labels, since the table's caption and placeholder make
  their purpose clear on screen.
- The empty state is a heading inside the table's body, so a screen reader
  reaching the table hears why it is empty.

patterns-application-ui-description-list.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as DescriptionListStories from './DescriptionList.stories'

<Meta of={DescriptionListStories} />

# Description List

The fields of a record, as terms and their details: a profile, an order,
an application. It is read-only; its editable twin is a settings form in
Form Layouts.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/description-list.json
```

## Columns

Term and details side by side, a line between rows, and an optional
action at the end of each row ("Update").

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## In a card

`isCard` puts the header in a top band and the list below it, inside one
border. With `layout="grid"`, fields run two to a row; `isWide` gives
long text and attachments the full width.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.InCard} />

## Stacked

Term over details, one field after another: for a sidebar or a narrow
panel.

<Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.Stacked} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `DescriptionItem[]` | – | Required. `{ term, details, action?, isWide? }` |
| `title` | node | – | |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons at the end of the header. |
| `layout` | `columns`, `grid`, `stacked` | `columns` | |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

<Controls of={DescriptionListStories.Columns} />

## Layout

- **It responds to its own width, not the viewport's.** Columns and grid
  are container queries: under 36rem of list width they stack, so the
  same list works in a main column, a sidebar and a phone.

  <Canvas of={DescriptionListStories.ColumnsNarrow} />

- Details wrap anywhere, so a long email address or URL never pushes the
  layout wide.

## Accessibility

- A real `<dl>`: a screen reader announces a list of terms and reads each
  detail with its term.
- Row actions sit in their own `<dd>` after the details. Give each one the
  field it acts on ("Update Email address"), hidden if you like, so a
  list of links is not six identical "Update"s.

patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--do.title: Patterns/Application UI/Form Layouts
patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as FormLayoutsStories from './FormLayouts.stories'

<Meta of={FormLayoutsStories} />

# Form Layouts

How the kit's fields are arranged into a form: sections with a heading
and a line of context, fields one or two to a row, and a row of actions
at the end. Three pieces: `FormSection`, `FormFullWidth` and
`FormActions`. The `<form>` element is yours.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/form-layouts.json
```

## Settings sections

A settings page. Each section's title and description sit in a column
beside its fields, sections are separated by a line, and one row of
actions saves the lot.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.SettingsSections} />

## Stacked in a card

One section on a card: the title above, fields two to a row, and the
actions in the card's bottom band.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.StackedInCard} />

## In a modal

A short form in a [Modal](?path=/docs/components-overlays-modal--docs).
The submit button sits in the modal's footer, outside the `<form>`, and
points at it with the `form` attribute, so Enter in a field and a click on
the button both submit.

<Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.InModal} />

## FormSection props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. An `h2` by default. |
| `description` | node | – | |
| `children` | node | – | The fields. Give each input `isFullWidth`. |
| `layout` | `split`, `stacked` | `split` | Split puts the intro in a column beside the fields. |
| `columns` | `1`, `2` | `1` | Two fields to a row. Wrap one in `FormFullWidth` to span the row. |
| `isCard` | boolean | `false` | |
| `footer` | node | – | Usually `FormActions`; the card's bottom band when `isCard`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2`, `3` | `2` | |

`FormActions` is a row of buttons aligned to the end: secondary actions
first, the primary one last.

<Controls of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

## Layout

- **Sections respond to their own width.** Split turns into stacked under
  48rem of section width, and two columns into one when the fields' side
  of the section (its whole width once stacked) is under 32rem. A form in
  a sidebar or a phone needs no extra props.
- **Sections are size containers**, so they take their width from where
  they sit. As a flex or grid item that would shrink to fit, give the
  section a width (`inline-size: 100%`), or it collapses.

  <Canvas of={FormLayoutsStories.Narrow} />

- Actions end-aligned, primary last: the same place in every form, where
  the eye and the Tab key end up.

## Accessibility

- Each section is a `<section>` with a heading, so the form's parts are in
  the page outline and a screen reader can jump between them.
- Group related checkboxes in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, as the
  Notifications section does; RadioGroup does this for you.
- Mark required fields with `required`. The field shows the asterisk and
  the browser enforces it; say in the description if most fields are
  optional instead.
- Never disable the submit button to show that a form is incomplete. Let
  it submit, and show what is missing next to each field.

import { Meta, Canvas, Story, ArgTypes } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { Anatomy, DocTab, DocTabs, DoDont, SpecTable, States, Status } from '../../../../.storybook/blocks' import * as NavSidebarStories from './NavSidebar.stories' # Nav Sidebar The app's main navigation, down the side of the screen: a header, links in named groups, and a footer. It can collapse to an icon rail. A pattern, one of the three pieces the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places (with the Top Bar and App Content); it was the Navigation/Sidebar component. ## Variants | Variant | Use for | | --- | --- | | Expanded | The default: icon, label and badge on every row. | | Collapsible (`isCollapsible`) | Apps where the content needs the width at times: a button in the header folds the sidebar to the rail. | | Rail (`isCollapsed` or `defaultCollapsed`) | Icons only, labels in tooltips. For tools the reader knows well. Every item needs an icon. | | Plain | No header or footer: a section's own navigation inside a larger layout. | ## Resources Copied into your project through the registry, like every pattern (not in the npm package): ```sh npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/nav-sidebar.json ``` - Source: [src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander/blob/main/src/components/patterns/application-ui/NavSidebar.tsx) - Spec: our own; uiguideline.com has no page for it - Behaviour: a plain `
`; the rail's labels use [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) - Figma: not in the library yet ## Anatomy In the rail, the header, the labels, the badges and the footer are hidden; each group starts with a rule instead of its label. ## Measurements Items are rows of the md control tier, flush against each other: a fill marks a row, not a gap. Expanded, the sidebar is 16rem wide. The rail is one square row plus the padding either side: `--control-md` plus twice `--space-2`. A long label is cut with an ellipsis. Give the sidebar the height to fill; its body scrolls when the items do not fit. ## Color Hover is an overlay, not a solid: in dark mode the sidebar's own surface is the same grey as `--accent`, so an opaque hover fill would vanish. ## States }, ]} > - **Current** is a `--selected` fill, a step past the hover fill so the two never read alike, plus medium weight for anyone who cannot tell the fills apart. It stays off the accent: where you are is not a call to action. - **Focus** is a 2px `--ring` outline drawn inside the row, so rows that sit flush do not cover each other's ring. - **Collapsed** is the rail; see Variants. ## API {/* Storybook's table does not scroll by itself on a phone. */}
Every other `
` attribute passes through. ## When to use Use a NavSidebar for an app's main navigation when it has more than five or so destinations, or will grow: the list runs down and does not wrap. Name groups by what is in them, keep labels to a word or two, and give every item an icon if the sidebar can collapse. } doCaption="Short labels, an icon on each, grouped under a few names." dont={} dontCaption="Long labels get cut, and with no icons there is nothing to show in the rail." /> ## When not to use - **For three to five sections of one page or object.** Use [Tabs](?path=/docs/components-navigation-tabs--docs) across the top. - **For actions.** A sidebar goes places. Put actions in [Buttons](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) or a [Menu](?path=/docs/components-navigation-menu--docs). - **On a phone, as is.** 16rem is most of a phone's width. Put it in a drawer, as the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) does. ## Accessibility - A `
` landmark named "Main"; rename it with `aria-label` when the page has another navigation. The current item has `aria-current="page"`. - Each group's label names its list through `aria-labelledby` ("Projects, list, 3 items"), and keeps doing so in the rail, where it is only visually hidden. Labels are not headings, so they do not compete with the page's outline. - In the rail each link keeps its name through `aria-label`, badge included ("Inbox, 12"), and a tooltip shows the same text on hover and on keyboard focus. - The collapse button is named "Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar" and carries `aria-expanded`. - Rows are 32px tall, 44px on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`).

patterns-application-ui-page-heading--do.name: Docs
patterns-application-ui-page-heading--do.title: Patterns/Application UI/Page Heading
patterns-application-ui-page-heading--do.content:
import { Meta, Canvas, Controls } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as PageHeadingStories from './PageHeading.stories'

<Meta of={PageHeadingStories} />

# Page Heading

The top of a page: where it is, what it is, and what you can do with it.
Breadcrumbs, title, a line of description, a few facts, the page's
actions, and optionally tabs for sections of the same page.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/page-heading.json
```

## Simple

Title, description and the page's main actions. Keep it to one primary
action; everything else is secondary.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## With breadcrumbs and meta

A record's page. Breadcrumbs say where it sits; meta holds short facts,
each optionally led by an icon or a Tag for a status. Rarely used actions
go in a Menu behind "More actions" so the row stays short.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithBreadcrumbsAndMeta} />

## With tabs

Sections of the same page as Tabs under the heading. The tab list's line
replaces the heading's own bottom border.

<Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.WithTabs} />

## Props

| Prop | Values | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | node | – | Required. |
| `description` | node | – | Muted, capped at 65 characters a line. |
| `breadcrumbs` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | – | Rendered small, above the title. |
| `meta` | `ReactNode[]` | – | A list of short facts. |
| `actions` | node | – | Buttons, a Menu. |
| `tabs` | node | – | A `Tabs` element. |
| `headingLevel` | `1`, `2` | `1` | 2 when the heading sits inside a larger page. |

Every other `<header>` attribute passes through.

<Controls of={PageHeadingStories.Simple} />

## Layout

- **Actions wrap, the title does not squeeze.** The title takes the row
  down to 20rem, then the actions drop underneath it, keeping their order.
  On a phone that means title first, then buttons.

  <Canvas of={PageHeadingStories.Narrow} />

- **Long titles break anywhere** rather than overflow, so a record named
  with one long word still fits.

## Accessibility

- The title is the page's `h1` by default. A page has one; pass
  `headingLevel={2}` if the heading sits under another.
- Breadcrumbs are a `nav` named "Breadcrumb", with the current page
  marked `aria-current="page"`.
- Meta is a list, so a screen reader announces how many facts there are.
  Icons in it are decorative; say the fact in words ("12 applicants").
- An icon-only action needs an `aria-label`, as on any Button.
